summary: A 1970 note by Jon Postel and Steve Crocker saying a new protocol is coming. It prepares the group for the upcoming host-to-host protocol.

eli5.summary: A heads-up that new rules for computers talking to each other are on the way.

questions: when did the new protocol come out
when was the first network meeting
subtitle: An announcement that a cleaner network protocol specification is coming

tldr.problem: The early ARPA Network needs a clear specification of the protocol that defines how computers will communicate.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC announces that a clean version is being prepared for release on April 28, 1970, with a discussion meeting scheduled at the SJCC on May 7 to clarify details and gather feedback.
tldr.outcome: This announcement kick-started the formal protocol discussion, leading to subsequent protocol proposals and refinements in the RFC series.

today: RFC 45 is a historical marker of the moment when the ARPA Network community committed to a formal protocol specification. This announcement set the stage for the subsequent protocol development that would define how the modern Internet works.

sections.title: Coming Specification
sections.content: Postel and Crocker announce that a clean version of the Network protocol is being prepared and will be released on April 28, 1970. The announcement emphasizes that this is a significant moment: the early ARPA Network participants have been discussing various protocol ideas, and this specification marks the start of formal, consistent rules for host-to-host communication.
sections.eli5: A team is making up the rules for how computers talk to each other. They will share these rules on April 28.

sections.title: Discussion Meeting
sections.content: The authors announce a discussion meeting at the Spring Joint Computer Conference (SJCC) in Atlantic City on Thursday, May 7. The purpose is for the authors to explain unclear details in the specification and for all participants to share feedback, suggestions, and implementation schedules. This meeting provides a chance for the network community to align before implementation.
sections.eli5: They will meet everyone in Atlantic City on May 7 to explain the rules and answer questions.

sections.title: Foundation for Network Coordination
sections.content: This brief note marks a turning point in the ARPA Network's development. Prior RFCs had been informal discussions and competing proposals. This announcement signals that the group is ready to standardize on a single protocol specification, necessary for the network to function as a unified system rather than a collection of incompatible site-to-site connections.
sections.eli5: Up until now, everyone had different ideas about how the network should work. Now they are all going to follow the same rules.
